clue.text: Clan burning coal for a month

parts.note: a sept is a branch of a clan, especially in Ireland or Scotland
an ember is a glowing piece of coal in a dying fire

explanation.surface: A Highland family gathers round the fire to see out a month of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: Join a clan, SEPT, to a glowing coal, EMBER. 'for' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth month of the calendar year is named from the Latin for seven.

clue.text: Prudence leaves soap on bath, we hear

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Prudence leaves soap on bath, we hear': SAGA (soap) + CITY (Bath) spells the answer exactly, so 'we hear' signals a homophone with no different spelling heard; 'leaves' also unexplained, possibly an OCR or feed garble, no reprint found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Prudence leaves soap on bath, we hear

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: one is a single individual

explanation.surface: One person props up a couple in an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts ONE below PR in the down light; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying face down is lying stretched out horizontally.

clue.text: Wantonly mistreat oxen in such culls?

indicators.note: wantonly means recklessly, without restraint, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Cruelly ill-treating cattle during a slaughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wantonly' rearranges MISTREAT OXEN IN; 'such' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Killings of whole herds or populations are destructions on a large scale.

explanation.surface: Trim the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: A bulldog clip is a strong spring clip for holding papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring stationery clamp bears the breed's name, and the breed is a stocky dog.

clue.text: Course that fills the squares in Italy

definitions.text: Course that fills the squares in Italy

parts.words: Course that fills the squares in Italy
parts.note: suggests a race or crowds filling piazzas, but the course is a dish of filled pasta squares

explanation.surface: A procession packs the piazzas of Italian towns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squares' seems to mean town piazzas; they are the small stuffed pasta parcels.
explanation.definitionFit: Small square envelopes of pasta with a filling are an Italian dish.

clue.text: Miner's body black and deprived of feeling

parts.note: the NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, the British miners' trade union
B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A coal miner, filthy and frozen after a shift, has lost all sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miner's body' looks like a worker's physique; it is the miners' union, the NUM, a British organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without sensation, as after cold or an anaesthetic, is the core sense of the word.

clue.text: How to take a bit from an Arab, for example?

definitions.text: How to take a bit from an Arab, for example?

parts.words: How to take a bit from an Arab, for example?
parts.note: reads as taking a share from a person, but the Arab is a horse and the bit is its mouthpiece

explanation.surface: A question about sharing something with a man from Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: An Arab is a breed of horse, and a bit is the metal bar in its mouth, removed when the tack comes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking off a horse's tack frees it of the straps and bit.

parts.note: a report is the noise of a gunshot, a bang
something on is arranged or scheduled, as in the game is on

explanation.surface: A news item is put together precisely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' is not a news story but the sound of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: British colloquial phrase meaning exactly right, spot on.

clue.text: That prickliest sort of Scottish club

indicators.note: sort here is a verb, to sort, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A thistle is the spikiest emblem of a Scottish club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' reorders THAT PRICKLIEST. Partick Thistle is a Glasgow football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A Glasgow football club named after the Partick district and the national emblem.

clue.text: Butter left inside? Rub it in

indicators.note: inside says the letter for left is placed within the animal

parts.note: a goat is something that butts, so in crosswords it can be called a butter

explanation.surface: A cook asks whether butter has been left in the dish, and is told to rub it in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' looks like the dairy spread but is an animal that butts, a GOAT; L goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow over a rival's misfortune is to make them feel it more, an idiom for taunting.

clue.text: Monster more dead than alive, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the phrase could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A creature from the deep is hauled ashore, more dead than alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges THAN ALIVE; 'more dead' is padding for the surface, a stock phrase the anagram fodder completes.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical sea beast of Job gave its name to any huge creature.

explanation.surface: A performer, thrilled, takes the ovation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uplifted is made glad, and a crowd that shouts approval greets a performer with hurrahs.

indicators.note: broadcast scatters seed widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A Canadian region goes live on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to broadcast' reads as radio work, which suits 'on air', but it is the anagram signal for ON AIR TO.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the ten Canadian provinces, home to Toronto and Ottawa.

clue.text: Smallest space for senator, say, to go about, converting society

definitions.text: Smallest space for senator, say, to go about

parts.note: turning someone is converting them to another side
a circle is a social group or set

explanation.surface: A politician turns about in a small space while winning over the members of a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'senator' is not a politician: the Vauxhall Senator was a British car, and a car needs a minimum diameter to make a U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Motoring term for the least diameter in which a vehicle can make a complete U-turn.

parts.note: to jar is to shake or jolt, to rock
a plant is an industrial works

explanation.surface: A glass container is made in a mountain-region works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jar' looks like a container noun but is the verb, to jolt; 'Alpine' is a noun, a mountain flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Small mountain flowers grown in rockeries are called alpines.

parts.note: reads as flimsy steel beams, but girders puns on garments that gird the middle of the body

explanation.surface: An engineer asks which central beams are the weakest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'girders' suggests steel beams; here it means things that gird the waist, and the skimpiest are thong underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: The skimpiest briefs cover almost nothing around the middle.

clue.text: With single reeds, they blow in the wind

definitions.text: With single reeds, they blow in the wind

parts.words: With single reeds, they blow in the wind
parts.note: reads like plants in a marsh, but the reeds are mouthpieces and the wind is the woodwind section of an orchestra

explanation.surface: Rushes sway in a breeze by a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: The reeds and wind suggest a marsh; they are a single-reed instrument's mouthpiece and the woodwind section.
explanation.definitionFit: Players of a single-reed woodwind instrument perform in an orchestra's wind section.

parts.note: suggests a punch bowl, but the vessel is a craft and the parties hint at breaking the ice

explanation.surface: A bowl that comes in handy at a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a drinks bowl; it is a craft, one that runs on frozen surfaces, and ice is what a party needs broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailed craft on runners travels across frozen lakes.

explanation.surface: Orders with agreements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To hire someone is to take them on, and to bind oneself by agreement is to pledge service.

clue.text: Endless dispute turns out to be mindless

indicators.note: turns out says the remaining letters are turned into a new order
endless drops the final letter of the word for dispute

explanation.surface: A row that never ends proves pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts DISPUTE to DISPUT, and 'turns out' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolish and thoughtless behaviour lacks intelligence.

explanation.surface: A pub drinker asks where to rest their mug.
explanation.walkthrough: TOPSIDE is a British cut of beef; read as TOP SIDE it is the team at the top, holding the trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean roasting cut comes from the upper thigh of beef, and a leading team winning a trophy is the best side.

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the word for girl

parts.note: litter is rubbish, refuse dropped in the street

explanation.surface: A young woman turns down showy finery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' looks like a verb, to decline, but it is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy sparkle and tinsel is a byword for cheap flashiness.

explanation.surface: Let fall a suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount, a drop of something, is a slight suggestion or vestige of it.

parts.note: even, as in smooth and level, means plain
a number is a song or piece in a performance

explanation.surface: A choir sings a piece in measured, even time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure but a musical item; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaccompanied single-line church music of the medieval Western liturgy goes by this name.

explanation.surface: A passenger sits at the back of a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear is to bring up and teach, and to coach is to instruct an athlete.

explanation.surface: A levy is charged on purchases and help alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs levy goods at the border, and an obligation performed is service owed.

explanation.surface: A clumsy apartment description.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking refinement is a want of style, and food without flavour is insipid.
